## Runs 6 then 7 — raw spot checks, onset stability, and the fan decision

This read uses only this session's TSVs via `hera.analysis.open_run`: sr1 = B_1–B_2, Rxx = sr1_X / (sr0_X / −1e6). Each run's raw trace precedes its derived spectrum. Neither run clipped; drain current stayed 9.81–9.94 nA and sample temperature 1.165–1.292 K. Negative four-terminal X excursions are retained, never rectified or log-clipped; no opposite-field symmetrization is available.

Run 6 (+3.2×10¹² cm⁻², calibrated D≈0) has candidate peaks near 7, 14, 22, and 29–30 T, with additional high-field harmonics. Run 7 (−1.2×10¹²) has stronger oscillations but overlapping low-frequency peaks and a ~12 T component whose origin is unresolved. Integer ratios alone cannot remove pockets: the harmonic screen must also respect the Luttinger sum and density trajectories. These traces do **not** establish stacking. F_L is 33.09 T on electrons and 12.41 T on holes before a global scale fit; the secondary CNP ridge in run 5 is an additional spatial-density confound.

**Onset sensitivity:** full-range polynomial subtraction produced censored low-frequency tracks, including background contamination. To locate the low-field onset independently of the large 8–10 T MR rise, the helper is also run on 0.6–5 T. On electrons, degrees 3/5/7 yield an uncensored ~1.00–1.01 T onset for the ~7.1 T track; its local sampling (~1 T and above, 10 mT) resolves that frequency and F_L. A 0.3–5 T degree-5 fit gives 1.02 T. The full-window censored result is retained as an extraction limitation, not interpreted as oscillations down to 0.3 T. Hole onset is lower but its available D≈0 densities stop at −1.27×10¹², inside the close-pocket exception regime (tetralayer investigation, Step 2). Choose electrons for the fan: the model's distinct high-density branches provide the more discriminating test. The onset and branch visibility must be checked again across the fan; no searched-and-absent pocket claim follows solely from this spot.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, resolve_channels
out={}
for rid,n in [(6,3.2),(7,-1.2)]:
 r=open_run(f'data/{rid}')
 plot_raw(r); plt.gcf().savefig(f'hera_scratch/spot{rid}_raw.png',dpi=130); plt.show()
 ch={c.cid:c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
 B=r.col('magnet_field'); I=r.col('sr0_X')/ch['sr0'].gain; R=r.col('sr1_X')/ch['sr1'].gain/I
 ix=np.argsort(B); B=B[ix]; R=R[ix]
 print('RUN',rid,'complete',r.complete,'interrupted',r.interrupted,'R',R.min(),R.max(),'I nA',I.min()*1e9,I.max()*1e9,'T',r.col('T_sample').min(),r.col('T_sample').max())
 dt=np.diff(r.col('time')); print('timing median sec',np.median(dt),'wall sec',np.ptp(r.col('time')))
 on=sdh_onset(R,B,b_lo=0.6,b_hi=5.0,r_full_scale=5000)
 print(on.summary())
 out[str(rid)]={'onset':float(on.onset_b),'tones':[{'f':float(t.freq),'onset':float(t.onset_b),'censored':bool(t.censored)} for t in on.tones]}
 fig,axs=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4))
 axs[0].plot(B,R); axs[0].axvline(on.onset_b,color='red'); axs[0].set(xlabel='B (T)',ylabel='Rxx (ohm)',title=f'run {rid}, n={n}, onset={on.onset_b:.3f} T')
 for lo in [1.0,1.5,2.0]:
  for deg in [3,5,7]:
   f,sp=sdh_fft(R[:,None],B,b_range=(lo,10),bg_degree=deg,nfft=4096,log=False)
   p,_=find_peaks(sp[0]); p=[k for k in p if 3<f[k]<55]; p=sorted(p,key=lambda k:sp[0,k],reverse=True)[:6]
   print('FFT',rid,'lo',round(lo,3),'degree',deg,'peaks',[(round(f[k],2),round(sp[0,k],3)) for k in p])
   axs[1].plot(f,sp[0],label=f'B>{lo:.2f}, deg {deg}',alpha=.6)
 axs[1].set(xlim=(0,55),xlabel='F (T)',ylabel='FFT amplitude'); axs[1].axvline(10.33916924*abs(n),color='black',ls='--',label='F_L'); axs[1].legend(fontsize=6)
 fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f'hera_scratch/spot{rid}_fft.png',dpi=130); plt.show()
Path('hera_scratch/spot_summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))

## Fan feasibility — model, onset audit, and cost floor

`landau-fan-vti` / `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count`: one electron fan at D≈0, n=2.8–3.2×10¹² cm⁻², B=1–6 T. The attached calculation prints the default censored onset and the local-window stability check, the ABAB model frequencies, both Nyquist checks, gate conversion, and the session-calibrated cost. It preserves the onset-window disagreement; branch absence will not be inferred below each branch's own usable onset. Absolute density remains geometry-prior and the two CNP ridges can represent distinct local densities, not demonstrated stacking domains.

ABAB predicts [6.04,22.91] to [7.31,25.78] T, ABCA predicts F_L=28.95–33.09 T. Resolution δF=1.20 T separates the predicted ABAB heavy tone from F_L; the smallest partner gets 5.03 periods only if visible to 1 T. Sampling protects the observed ~130 T high-field content against folding into that pocket band: Δ(1/B)=0.003788 T⁻¹, Nyquist 132 T. This costs 221 rows, versus ~100 if only F_L were considered. The n-axis floor, including 20% scale uncertainty, is 11 points (Δn=0.04×10¹²); 2431 points total. At the native scale the grid has >8 samples per F_L period.

The deliberately narrow density window preserves the high-density template separation and shares n=3.2 with run 6. It excludes the CNP and hole side, whose accessible densities lie in ambiguous close-pocket regimes; covering n=2.7 at five partner periods requires ~9 T and ~22 additional minutes of bare ramp, while n≤2.6 cannot attain five partner periods at this onset within the 10 T cap. A broad CNP-to-electron map would add about 15,500 points (~15 hours with margin) without meeting this FS-count period criterion at its low-density end. The current short density span can reject simple harmonics but may still leave an ABAB/ABCB/adjacent-N fork; compare ABAB and trilayer overlays before a region verdict.

## HERA — high-density electron Landau fan for the stacking test

> **05:25** · D~0 electron fan; n=2.8..3.2e12 cm^-2 (11); B=1->6 T (221 uniform-1/B rows); 10 nA, 3 s dwell, Si=0; hold 6 T · **ETA ~08:55** (≈3h30m)

Proceed under the recorded E1 grant with `landau-fan-vti`, following `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` Steps 2–5. Gates A/B remain green (measure 18/32 and handoff 44/46); Gate C passed in runs 0–3. Runs 6/7 and their raw-first analysis in ana 14–17 establish oscillations but leave harmonic/pocket ambiguity. Electrons reach the model's discriminating density range; the stronger hole signal is limited to |n|≤1.27×10¹² by the committed TG fence and has overlapping tones. Use run-5 region-A calibration (ratio measured, absolute scale geometry-prior, D≈0 inferred from ridge symmetry), and retain the second CNP ridge as a spatial-density uncertainty.

**Resolution and coverage.** The local-window `sdh_onset` audit of run 6 gives 1.003–1.010 T across polynomial degrees 3/5/7; start at 1.00 T, rounding down. Full-record detrending gives a censored onset and is documented as a background-extraction limitation; this fan does not establish sub-1-T absence. The model predicts ABAB tones 6.04/22.91 T at n=2.8 and 7.31/25.78 T at n=3.2, compared with ABCA F_L=28.95–33.09 T. At 6 T the low-density partner has 5.03 periods and δF=1.20 T; if its actual onset rises across density, downgrade the period/absence claim. Use 221 uniform-1/B rows (Δ1/B=0.003788 T⁻¹, Nyquist 132 T) to protect against run 6's observed high-frequency content, plus 11 density points (Δn=0.04×10¹², the ray-Nyquist floor with 20% scale allowance). This is 2431 points. The narrow 2.8–3.2 window includes the spot-check anchor, excludes CNP/holes, and may leave an adjacent-N/ABCB fork if the short branch trajectories cannot distinguish models. CNP-to-3.2 coverage at the same sampling would add ~15,500 points (~15 h including margin) while violating the five-partner-period criterion at low n. Lowering the electron edge to 2.7 requires about 9 T for five partner periods; ≤2.6 cannot meet that criterion below the 10 T cap at this onset.

**Acquisition and price.** Fixed 10 nA drive, sr1=20 µV (2 kΩ nominal full scale), sr0=20 mV, inherited τ=0.3 s / 24 dB, point dwell=3 s (10τ). Run 6 has |R|≤131 Ω through 6 T; allow a deliberately conservative 10× low-density/MR envelope (~1.31 kΩ), still below the 1.8 kΩ rail checkpoint. This envelope is empirical rather than a guaranteed bound, so monitor every row. Gates span TG 0.8690–0.9836 V and BG 1.0180–1.1663 V; Si stays 0 V. Initial 0→1 T positioning costs 7.3 min; total 0→6 T costs 43.8 min at 0.137 T/min. Run 5 measured ~0.10 s read overhead at NPLC=1; budget 3.20 s/point including paired gates and added vaporizer read, plus ~0.32 s gate flyback, 3 s magnet settle and 1 s slow delay per row. Total ≈3.16 h, priced with 10% margin. Actual first rows will update it. No pacing, validator, or operating-limit changes.

**Checkpoints and endpoint.** Preconditions print expected/actual validators, temperature freshness/base state, heater ranges, Si/output state, magnet state, contact map, drive, settling and gate pacing before writes. Inspect the first three completed rows for rails, leakage, drain continuity, noise and phase; continue only if clean. Recheck every 30 min, and after reaching 3 T compare n=3.2 with run 6, allowing only the expected sensitivity/grid change; abandon if the fan loses the spot-check structure. All recorded channels are plotted. Per-point guards stop on >1 nA gate current, approaching sr1 rail, lost base T, or drain discontinuity; log freshness and actual field are checked per row. If interrupted, hold and read actual state before any next move; a kernel interrupt does not stop an in-progress VTI supply ramp (rig-card rule). On success hold B=6 T and the last gate point for analysis. Re-form the raw map first, then FFT/window stability, harmonic/Luttinger tests, and both ABAB/trilayer overlays before any B_1–B_2 region verdict.
